data.cultural_impact: Maxwell was a Anglicized version of the Scottish name Maccolm or Macquhalium, which translates to 'son of the greatest hero'. The name became popular in England during the Middle Ages and was also used for persons of significant power and authority, such as nobles and clergymen. In modern times, Maxwell has been associated with successful and influential figures such as James Clerk Maxwell, a renowned physicist, Mathew Maxwell and Tim Maxwell, prominent sports personalities, and Maxwell Perkins, a distinguished literary agent.
